title: DeSantis Urges Other States to Copy Florida's H-1B University Hiring Freeze
excerpt: Florida has barred its 12 public universities from new H-1B hires until January 5, 2027. Governor Ron DeSantis is now presenting that pause as a model for other states, while faculty warn it will cost campuses scarce research and medical talent.
body:
• Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has urged other states to stop hiring foreign workers through the H-1B visa program at public universities, presenting Florida's own hiring pause as a model.
  • Florida's Board of Governors voted 17-2 to halt new H-1B hires across the state's 12 public universities until January 5, 2027; existing H-1B employees and renewals are not affected.
  • Faculty and researchers say most university H-1B hires are physicians, Ph.D. scientists and STEM faculty, and warn the pause will push top candidates to competing states.
  • For Indian professionals and students: the freeze blocks new university jobs in Florida only — it does not cancel existing H-1B status, renewals, or private-sector H-1B hiring.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has called on other U.S. states to follow Florida and stop hiring foreign workers through the H-1B visa program at public universities, according to Times Now World. In a statement posted to social media, DeSantis highlighted Florida's restriction as a model, arguing that prioritizing domestic graduates is essential when young Americans face difficulty securing entry-level positions.

The appeal extends a policy DeSantis set in motion in October 2025, when he directed the Florida Board of Governors — the body overseeing the state's 12 public universities — to "pull the plug" on H-1B hiring. At that news conference, reported by The Chronicle of Higher Education, he said universities had abused the program for nonspecialized roles, citing a computer-application coordinator from China, an assistant swim coach from Spain, and a psychologist from the United Kingdom.

"We need to make sure our citizens here in Florida are first in line for job opportunities."

— Ron DeSantis, Governor of Florida

What Florida Actually Did

Rather than a permanent ban, Chancellor Ray Rodrigues proposed a one-year pause, pointing to the federal $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions announced in September 2025, Florida Trend reported. Rodrigues said the price tag called for a study of how universities use the program, whether hiring is in areas of "strategic need," and whether H-1B salaries match market rates. On March 2, the Board of Governors voted 17-2 to stop hiring new public university employees under H-1B visas until January 5, 2027.

The moratorium does not affect existing H-1B employees or renewals. Policy experts told Florida Trend the pause appears to bar even candidates who already hold an H-1B with another U.S. employer. "This temporary suspension and study give us time to make informed policy decisions," Rodrigues said in a statement quoted by Florida Trend.

Why Universities Use H-1B Differently

Universities are not typical H-1B employers. Under federal rules, institutions of higher education are exempt from the annual H-1B cap and lottery, a distinction explained by the University of California, Berkeley International Office and by UC San Diego's H-1B guidance, which notes H-1B status is for specialty occupations requiring specialized knowledge and at least a bachelor's degree in a related field. That exemption lets campuses file at any time of year for faculty, researchers and physicians.

Public universities accounted for about 6% of Florida's more than 10,000 approved H-1B applications last fiscal year, Florida Trend reported. Inside Higher Ed put Florida's 12 public universities at 637 approved visas in fiscal 2025, with the University of Florida the largest user.

The Other Side: Faculty Warn of Lost Talent

Faculty have pushed back, arguing campus data do not support a cheap-labor narrative. An Institute for Progress analysis of first-time petitions from 2017 to 2022, cited by Florida Trend, found at least one in four were for physicians, Ph.D. scientists or STEM faculty, 96% held a master's, doctoral or professional degree, and about 16% were born in India and 22.5% in China.

"The H-1B program is routinely used at any university in order to bring the best talent," David Simmons, a University of South Florida engineering professor and faculty senate president, told Florida Trend. "Any pause in the ability to hire folks in those world-class areas of expertise leaves Florida behind competing states."

What This Means for Indian Readers

For Indian faculty, researchers, physicians and graduating students, the line is narrow but important: a Florida public university cannot start a new H-1B hire during the pause, even if you already hold H-1B status elsewhere, while private universities, public universities in other states, and private employers are not bound by Florida's rule. Existing Florida holders can continue and renew. DeSantis also criticized Optional Practical Training, but OPT is federal and Florida's pause does not change it.

What Happens Next

The pause runs to January 5, 2027, and the board's study will shape whether it is lifted, extended or replaced with exceptions for medicine and engineering. Texas has adopted a similar freeze through May 31, 2027, according to Inside Higher Ed — a sign the model DeSantis is promoting is already spreading.
